overview: Product Traceability and Recall Readiness addresses operational records arrive through different systems, supervisors reconstruct evidence manually, and decisions are difficult to audit in manufacturing operations. The first proof of value uses batch genealogy, source material lots and customer dispatches. It produces a reviewed operational recommendation and a traceable decision record. The commercial success measure is time to isolate affected lots, established from customer baseline data before any improvement is claimed.

scope:
Delivery model: Redington or approved implementation partner, eligibility and staffing pending confirmation.
Duration: Discovery and design first; pilot and rollout durations depend on data access and scope; no fixed commitment.
1) Discover source quality and baseline: batch genealogy, source material lots and customer dispatches; define time to isolate affected lots and data-processing boundary.
2) Design control points, security and connector contracts; obtain owner approval from Plant Manager / Operations Excellence Director.
3) Implement one bounded workflow, instrument missing-data exceptions and system-of-record write-back.
4) Test positive, negative, privilege, partial-data and rollback cases including line-by-line reconciliations against known business transactions.
5) Review KPI in the pilot, document evidence, perform training and agree transition.
